text:
marta: Pushed a profiling dump from last night's CI run + a short proposal to tweak how we classify workloads for continuous batching. Link: https://internal.ci/reports/2151234567.zip

marta: TL;DR: our current length-bucket + decode-rate bins lead to very uneven batch formation for the 'medium-long fast-decode' traffic. p95 latency spikes & KV thrash. I sketched new thresholds and token-budget caps.

jason: looked through the trace. agree there's a p95 cliff when medium prompts + high decode-rate mix with cached KV misses. can you paste the numbers?

marta: paste of key numbers:
```
- overall p50/p95: 48ms / 420ms
- cohort: short-fast (<=64 tokens, >800 tok/s): p95 62ms
- cohort: medium-fast (65-256, >800 tok/s): p95 620ms <-- bad
- cohort: long-slow (>256, <400 tok/s): p95 340ms
- KV miss rate correlated with medium-fast: 22% (vs 6% baseline)
- GPU util on impacted pods: 89% with frequent kernel flips
```

li: 620ms is huge. Is the kernel selector thrashing between fp16-quant kernels and the fallback full-kernel?

marta: yes — trace shows frequent kernel rebinds when batch contains mixed decode-rates. Also admission tries to microbatch but token-budget target is too loose, so we end up admitting many small items causing many tiny kernel launches.

nate: proposal idea: reclassify by both length and sustained decode-rate (tokens/sec over first 20 tokens). enforce token-budget per-batch = min(global_budget, cohort_target) and a hard lower bound on admission wait for medium-fast cohort to allow grouping.

sam: can you show the classifier rule you want? I'd like to see pseudocode we can put into the admission path.

marta: sure, rough proto we tested locally:
```
# compute decode_rate = tokens_generated_in_first_20s / time_seconds
if prompt_len <= 64 and decode_rate >= 800:
  cohort = "short-fast"
elif 65 <= prompt_len <= 256 and decode_rate >= 800:
  cohort = "medium-fast"
elif prompt_len > 256 or decode_rate < 400:
  cohort = "long-slow"
else:
  cohort = "medium-slow"

# batch token budget selection
batch_token_budget = min(global_token_budget, cohort_budget_map[cohort])
# cohort_budget_map: short-fast=512, medium-fast=384, medium-slow=256, long-slow=128
```

jason: those cohort_budget_map numbers seem reasonable. curious why medium-fast has higher budget than long-slow?

marta: medium-fast has high decode-rate so we prefer larger token budget to amortize kernel init costs and keep decode steady. long-slow are already high seq so we favor smaller batches to avoid latency blowups.

li: one risk: increasing budget for medium-fast may raise KV cache pressure and cause more misses. any mitigation?

marta: two mitigations in the patch: 1) prefetch KV for cohort when we detect >15% chance of a KV miss based on recent hit histogram; 2) if KV miss rate > 15% for 30s, dynamically drop cohort_budget by 25% and route to kernel-variant optimized for sparse KV.

perf-bot: Perf regression alert: medium-fast cohort p95 jumped from 140ms -> 620ms on 2026-03-15 03:12 UTC after deploy f16a3. Rolling this back reduces p95 by ~55%.

nate: good to know. sounds like a deploy-time kernel change exposed the governance gap. we should add a canary test that mixes decode-rate variations to validate kernel selector stability.

sam: also can we add a tracing tag for "cohort" into the span so perf dashboards can slice without extra joins? will help SLO alerts.

marta: yeah I'll add trace tag + metric (cohort.kv_miss_rate) and a small e2e canary. I've got a branch with the classifier + dynamic-budget: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/4329

jason: quick checklist before we ship:
- add cohort span tag (sam)
- add canary test exercising mixed decode rates (nate)
- add KV-prefetch toggle + fallback (marta)
- baseline perf run (perf-bot)

li: one more: add a short unit test that simulates kernel selector churn when given mixed decode-rate batch contents. we can assert kernel_bind_count <= 2 for budget >= X.

marta: will do. I'll update the PR today. thanks folks :thumbsup:

jason: awesome. please post perf run link here once available.

marta: will do — I'll also attach the diff for the classifier so you can eyeball thresholds.

nate: nice work. if canary looks good let's land and roll to staged.

sam: agreed. :rocket:
